stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: Anthropic's S-1 filing reveals a significant reliance of generative AI data centers on natural gas.
The intense competition for power and suitable data center locations is a major operational challenge for AI firms.
This highlights the growing, often overlooked, environmental and energy infrastructure demands of the AI boom.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a language model.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to major AI frameworks like transformers and the Llama family.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'llama'.
The content is relevant to the ongoing development and benchmarking of large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics
stories.author: Richard Lawler
bullet_points: OpenAI has announced three new 'major' scientific discoveries across mathematics, computer science, and physics.
This follows a recent release of hundreds of manuscripts claiming solutions to long-standing mathematical problems.
A key change is the inclusion of external experts, described as 'shepherds,' to guide the validation of these results.

stories.title: Microsoft offers to buy out a quarter of its workforce
stories.author: Nick Indge
bullet_points: Microsoft is initiating workforce reduction efforts by offering buyouts to employees.
The layoffs/offers are targeted at employees across major global hubs including the US, Canada, India, and the UK.
This signals a potential significant restructuring or cost-cutting measure within the tech giant.

stories.title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Highway thieves successfully stole $100M in data center equipment.
The theft was facilitated by sophisticated GPS spoofing technology.
The incident highlights critical vulnerabilities in modern logistics and supply chain security.

stories.title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
stories.author: Kilian Q. Weinberger
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of traditional retrieval methods (lexical/embedding matching) where strong generators cannot recover missing information.
Introduces DecisionRAG, a novel approach that integrates language model capabilities into the retrieval process.
Achieves this integration using decision models that evaluate candidate branches in a single forward pass without token generation.

stories.title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
stories.author: Ying Sun
bullet_points: Introduces NPC-RubricBench, a new phase-aware benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs across the entire longitudinal cancer care continuum.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which typically focus on isolated clinical encounters rather than evolving patient journeys.
Uses real-world longitudinal records of 405 patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma to validate the benchmark's utility in specialty medicine.

stories.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
stories.author: Massih-Reza Amini
bullet_points: Introduces 'Reva,' a system for real-time vulnerability detection in code.
Leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to act as security experts by performing contextual probing and analysis.
Addresses the growing challenge of code generation speed outpacing traditional developer review capabilities.

stories.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
stories.author: Shyamal Buch
bullet_points: Introduces Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) to bridge the gap between world understanding and physical action in robotics.
Leverages a large, pretrained vision-language model (27B parameters) for initial reasoning and world knowledge.
Uses simulation-based fine-tuning (Supervised Fine-Tuning and GRPO) to teach the model the necessary motor control skills.

stories.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
stories.author: Shyamal Buch
bullet_points: Introduces Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) to bridge the gap between world understanding and physical robot control.
Leverages large pretrained vision-language models (27B parameters) for initial world reasoning.
Uses simulation (supervised fine-tuning and GRPO) to teach the model the necessary motor skills for task execution.

stories.title: AI Agents Have the Keys to Your Computer. I Spent 8 Months Building an Antivirus for Them.
stories.author: id_1
bullet_points: AI agents with terminal access pose a significant security risk, capable of executing system-level commands.
The article details an 8-month project focused on building an antivirus solution specifically designed to counter these advanced AI agents.
The core threat involves agents being able to install packages, run scripts, and spawn child processes on a computer.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial supported model is Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech functionality.
The feature boasts high performance, streaming audio over 100x faster than real-time on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the capabilities of the Ollama ecosystem with advanced multimodal AI.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, via Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is currently available for free on Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses deployment and security concerns for AI agent development.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports integration with Ollama.
This integration allows users to utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
Ollama functions as a third-party gateway provider for this functionality.

stories.title: Data center backlash is uniting America
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: The rapid expansion of data centers is emerging as a significant political issue.
Local communities nationwide are mounting opposition to the construction of these facilities.
Data center infrastructure and associated costs are becoming a key topic in congressional debates for 2026.

stories.title: The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing
stories.author: Mia Sato
bullet_points: The RealReal is enhancing its bot defense system to prevent misuse by AI agents.
The update follows reports that AI agents were exploiting the retailer's item reserve system.
This highlights the growing challenge of automated scraping and bot abuse in e-commerce.

stories.title: Apple acknowledges iPhone Duo display ‘issue’ after reports of cracked screens
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple has officially acknowledged a display issue affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units.
The reported problem includes cracked and broken inner screens, sometimes showing a bright line.
The issue was brought to light following user reports and subsequent media coverage.

stories.title: Apple reveals updated iPad mini with a bigger OLED screen for $700
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Apple has released an updated iPad mini.
The key hardware upgrade is the inclusion of a larger OLED screen.
The new model is priced at $700, which Apple touts as a major line update.

stories.title: Musk accuses Ukraine of violating Starlink terms with deadly drone strikes
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Musk alleges Ukraine violated Starlink terms through drone strikes.
Ukraine denies misuse of the commercial Starlink service.
Starshield operations are reported to be back to normal by Ukrainian sources.

stories.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces FLORE, a new framework designed for learning force-reactive locomotion and manipulation in humanoids.
Addresses the challenge that many real-world tasks require controlling contact forces, which kinematics alone cannot specify.
The system utilizes robot-free demonstrations captured via force-sensing grippers and wearable body trackers.

stories.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
stories.author: Ari Juels
bullet_points: Addresses the growing vulnerability of traditional Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) systems to AI agent bypasses.
Introduces the concept of Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop (I-HITL) to enforce strict human approval.
I-HITL ensures an AI agent can only initiate critical actions with explicit human consent.

stories.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
stories.author: Chunhua Shen
bullet_points: The research evaluates frontier multimodal LLMs (like GPT-6-Astra) for robot control without task-specific training.
It compares the capabilities of these LLM-based agents against established post-trained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Model (WAM) policies.
The evaluation is conducted using the EBench framework under standardized visual and proprioceptive observation protocols.

stories.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Addresses the inefficiency of Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) which require many decoding rounds.
Introduces 'dSpark,' a schedule distillation method to improve generation speed in dLLMs.
Focuses on optimizing the commitment strategy—deciding when to commit to a token based on its predictive utility for future tokens.

stories.title: Game theory of academic effort and hiring in the age of AI
stories.author: Peter S. Park
bullet_points: The rise of accessible AI challenges traditional metrics for assessing academic expertise.
Previously, high-quality research papers served as a reliable signal of deep understanding in fields like mathematics.
AI lowers the cost of producing 'strong theoretical results,' undermining their reliability as hiring/evaluation signals.

stories.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
stories.author: Hanwen Jiang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Auto-Research Arena,' a new multi-target benchmark for evaluating autonomous research systems.
The benchmark is designed to support meaningful research progress in language modeling by separating result admissibility from improvement.
It allows for diverse research objectives within a shared environment, considering model quality and resource constraints.

stories.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces FLORE, a new framework designed for learning force-reactive locomotion and manipulation in humanoids.
Addresses the complexity of real-world tasks requiring coordinated control of contact forces across multiple body parts, which kinematics alone cannot solve.
Utilizes robot-free demonstrations captured via force-sensing grippers and wearable body trackers for training data.

stories.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
stories.author: Weiwen Liu
bullet_points: Focuses on the evolution of foundation models from information generation to digital work execution.
Addresses the research gap regarding how AI agents reliably complete complex, delegated tasks across various tools and workflows.
Proposes a new, work-centric system-level perspective for designing and optimizing these work agents.

stories.title: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?
stories.author: David Nordström
bullet_points: The research investigates the uncertainty quantification of 3D reconstruction models like VGGT, which currently output deterministic predictions without error metrics.
The study tests if the model's internal features can implicitly signal when its predicted camera poses are incorrect, even if the model itself doesn't report uncertainty.
Using a linear probe on frozen VGGT features, the researchers successfully predict pose failure on difficult image pairs where the model performs poorly.

stories.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Addresses the inefficiency of Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) which require many decoding rounds.
Introduces 'dSpark,' a schedule distillation method to improve generation speed by optimizing token commitment.
Highlights that efficient generation depends on strategically choosing tokens that maximize future predictability, not just immediate predictability.

stories.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
stories.author: Benjamin Van Durme
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of sparse outcome rewards in long-horizon language model agents.
Introduces FOCUS, a Reinforcement Learning (RL) method designed to improve critic network accuracy.
Mitigates high computational costs associated with estimating intermediate state values via repetitive sampling.

stories.title: Preserve to Expand: Source-Aware Adaptation and Model Merging for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR
stories.author: Ravi Shekhar
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of expanding multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems to new languages.
Proposes using connector-based Speech LLMs where a trainable connector interfaces with a frozen LLM.
Investigates target-update construction and model merging strategies to adapt the connector while preserving performance on existing languages.

stories.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces dSpark, a new schedule distillation technique for Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs).
Addresses the inefficiency of dLLMs, which require many decoding rounds for token generation.
Proposes that efficient generation depends on strategically committing to tokens, balancing predictability with contextual gain.

stories.title: Quantifying Claim Smoothing by LLM Research Agents
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: LLMs used for synthesizing large document collections can produce reports that sound highly confident.
The research identifies a phenomenon called 'claim smoothing,' where LLMs fail to accurately reflect underlying source material.
This smoothing occurs because the models collapse diverse and potentially conflicting source evidence into a single, coherent narrative.

stories.title: SEMA-Auto: Sighted and Efficient Multi-Turn Attack with Autonomy
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: SEMA-Auto addresses limitations in existing LLM jailbreak attacks by bridging the gap between static and interactive methods.
It overcomes the inefficiency of static planners (which ignore victim replies) and the high cost of interactive generators (which require complex in-loop evaluators).
The proposed method is described as 'sighted and efficient,' suggesting a novel approach to multi-turn adversarial prompting.

stories.title: Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
stories.author: Wu Yuan
bullet_points: The research investigates the capability of the JEV decision model versus schema-constrained Qwen Flash for clinical trial prescreening.
The core task involves distinguishing between unmet medical conditions and insufficient evidence using patient records and predefined criteria.
The evaluation was conducted on 2,048 test pairs using datasets derived from MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, emphasizing Zero Data Retention.

stories.title: Quantitative Generalization Bounds for Multi-Layer Transformers: A Few Long Strings can Beat Many Short Ones
stories.author: Michael Hahn
bullet_points: The paper addresses the theoretical gap in understanding how Transformer models generalize to complex, unseen data.
It proposes quantitative generalization bounds, suggesting that model performance depends on multiple axes of generalization.
The findings imply that a few long training examples can be more effective than many short ones for certain tasks.

stories.title: From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing
stories.author: Yang Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the miscalibration issue of self-confidence scores in LLMs and MLLMs.
Proposes a unified statistical framework to compare direct human auditing with LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.
Examines the practical trade-offs between the quality of LLM judging and the cost/efficiency of evaluation methods.

stories.title: Roblox downloaded 145GB models from us (including adult content) without asking
stories.author: choult
bullet_points: Roblox reportedly downloaded a large volume (145GB) of models from a user.
The downloaded content allegedly included adult material.
The download occurred without the user's explicit consent or knowledge.

stories.title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis Is False [pdf]
stories.author: vok
bullet_points: The news concerns a mathematical/theoretical computer science finding: the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) has been shown to be false.
This is a high-level, academic discovery, suggesting a potential shift in complexity theory.
The announcement is presented alongside other discoveries in mathematics, computer science, and physics, indicating broad theoretical impact.

stories.title: About the compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs
stories.author: support.apple.com via freddyb
bullet_points: The news concerns the compromise of eMudhra intermediate Certificate Authorities (CAs).
This is a significant cybersecurity incident affecting digital trust infrastructure.
The report from Lobsters indicates a vulnerability or breach within the CA system.

stories.title: Slopsquatting: 1 in 5 AI Code Samples Recommends a Package That Doesn't Exist
stories.author: debashish_ghosal
bullet_points: AI code generation tools are frequently suggesting non-existent or fictional software packages.
The issue, termed 'Slopsquatting,' highlights a significant reliability flaw in current large language models (LLMs) used for coding.
This points to a need for better validation and grounding mechanisms in AI-assisted software development.
